scope: non-implementer source review of assessment/summary/verify lifecycle lock
checks: Assessment CLI acquires the experiment lifecycle lock before readJsonl/assess/publish and retains it until publication returns; library export does not acquire a lock.
Selection resolves actual result read path and output parent with realpath and uses path.relative containment, covering existing symlink aliases without relying on substring prefixes.
Generic temporary result/input/output files outside this experiment do not participate in its lifecycle.
Summary CLI wraps buildSummary plus exclusive publication or check as one operation. The buildSummary library function remains unlocked for callers already holding the lock.

verifyExperiment outer wrapper takes verify lock only for non-preflight; original validation, enumeration and publication stay together. Preflight remains unlocked to avoid deadlock inside active runner; preflight cannot write manifest.
The same lock sits outside results so it does not become an immutable result artifact; failed callbacks preserve error and ownership-checked finally release. No automatic stale lock removal added.
limitations: Tests use real unchanged CLI modules in owned temporary dependency trees and synthetic empty assessment/report fixtures.
Active holdout is represented by a real filesystem lock with synthetic owner metadata. This is not a model holdout run.
Busy manifest refusal is tested before preflight. After release the intentionally absent freeze stops verification immediately, so no historical verifier or scoring chain executes.
The publication barrier instruments fs.promises.link and delegates to the real native hard link after release; it does not replace the publication result.
Concurrency requires cooperating entry points; this review does not claim protection against malicious filesystem symlink races or external writers ignoring the lock.
